questions.question: In the animal kingdom, which of the following phyla includes animals with a segmented body?
questions.solution:
The phylum Annelida includes animals with a segmented body (metamerism).
  • Examples include earthworms and leeches.
  • While Arthropoda also shows segmentation, Annelida is the classic example defined by its ring-like segments.

questions.question: What cellular structure is responsible for breaking down and recycling cellular components and molecules?
questions.solution:
Lysosomes are responsible for breaking down and recycling cellular components.
  • They contain hydrolytic enzymes that digest waste materials and cellular debris, earning them the nickname 'suicidal bags' of the cell.

questions.question: A little child is a very picky eater and hates drinking milk and milk products. When he lost his baby tooth, permanent teeth took a very long time to come up in its place. What could be the probable reason behind this?
questions.solution:
The child likely has a Calcium Deficiency.
  • Calcium is a critical mineral for the development and maintenance of teeth and bones. Milk and dairy products are primary sources of calcium, and a lack of intake can lead to delayed tooth eruption.

questions.question: What is the primary role of autotrophic organisms in an ecosystem?
questions.option_3: Preying on other organisms for food
questions.option_4: Producing organic matter from inorganic substances
questions.solution:
The primary role of autotrophic organisms (like plants) is producing organic matter from inorganic substances.
  • Using photosynthesis, they convert water, carbon dioxide, and sunlight into glucose (organic matter), forming the base of the food chain.

questions.question: Which of the following are the amounts of nutrients in a keto diet?
questions.option_1: High carbohydrate, proper amount of protein and low fat
questions.option_2: High protein and fat, carbohydrates in a low amount
questions.option_3: Only taking high number of vitamins and minerals
questions.option_4: High amount of fat, adequate protein and low carbohydrate
questions.solution:
A keto diet is characterized by high amount of fat, adequate protein, and low carbohydrate.
  • The goal is to move the body's metabolism away from burning glucose and toward burning fat and ketones (ketosis).

questions.question: To remain healthy and disease free, taking a balanced diet is very important. A balanced diet is:
questions.option_1: a diet that contains adequate amount of carbohydrates
questions.option_2: a diet that contains adequate amount of protein and fat
questions.option_3: a diet that contains sufficient amount of all the nutrients that the human body needs to grow properly
questions.option_4: a diet that contains appreciable number of vitamins and minerals
questions.solution: A balanced diet is a diet that contains sufficient amount of all the nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water) that the human body needs to grow and function properly.

questions.question:
A coastal area was flooded with sea water and resulted in heavy salt deposits in the nearby area. After a few days, it was observed that many plants died. Based on these statements, which of the following is the most probable cause of the plant deaths?

A. Plants died due to infection from sea water borne germs.

B. Plants died due to absence of sunlight.

C. Plants died due to plasmolysis in the plant cells.

D. Plants died because they were eaten by sea organisms.
questions.solution:
The most probable cause is plasmolysis in the plant cells.
  • Sea water is hypertonic (higher salt concentration) compared to the inside of the plant cells. Through osmosis, water leaves the plant cells to balance the concentration, causing the protoplasm to shrink away from the cell wall, which eventually kills the plant.

questions.question: Which of the following can be a basis of difference between a salamander and a house-wall lizard apart from their habitat?
questions.solution:
The presence or absence of scales on the skin is the distinguishing factor.
  • A salamander is an amphibian and has moist, scale-less skin.
  • A house-wall lizard is a reptile and has dry, scaly skin. Both are cold-blooded and typically lay eggs.

questions.question: Epilepsy is a disorder that affects which of the following parts of the human body?
questions.solution:
Epilepsy is a central nervous system (neurological) disorder in which brain cell activity becomes disrupted.
  • This disruption causes seizures or periods of unusual behavior, sensations, and sometimes loss of awareness.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles possesses their own DNA and can synthesise protein for their functions?
questions.solution:
Chloroplasts (along with mitochondria) possess their own DNA and ribosomes.
  • This allows them to synthesize some of their own proteins independently of the cell's nucleus, a trait explained by the endosymbiotic theory.

questions.question: Which of the given options is rod-shaped, carries genetic information, is visible only at cell division and is present in the nucleus?
questions.solution:
Chromosomes are rod-shaped structures found in the nucleus that carry genetic information (DNA).
  • They are only clearly visible under a microscope during cell division, when the chromatin condenses.

questions.question: The microscopic channels, which traverse the cell walls of plant cells and some algal cells, enabling transport and communication between them is called:
questions.solution:
Plasmodesmata are microscopic channels that traverse the cell walls of plant cells.
  • They facilitate transport and communication by allowing the movement of molecules and signals directly between the cytoplasms of adjacent cells.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement.
questions.option_1: Functional segments of DNA are called genes.
questions.option_2: Chromosomes are composed of DNA and carbohydrates.
questions.option_3: DNA molecules contain the information necessary for constructing and organising cells.
questions.option_4: The chromatin material gets organised into rod-shaped chromosomes only when the cell is about to divide.
questions.solution:
The incorrect statement is: 'Chromosomes are composed of DNA and carbohydrates.'
  • Chromosomes are actually composed of DNA and proteins (specifically histones). They do not contain carbohydrates as a structural component.

questions.question: The cytoplasmic zone surrounding the Golgi complex possesses no cell organelles. This zone of clear cytoplasm is called:
questions.solution:
The zone of exclusion is the region of clear cytoplasm surrounding the Golgi complex that is devoid of other organelles like ribosomes or mitochondria.
  • This area is thought to facilitate the specialized trafficking of vesicles to and from the Golgi.

questions.question:
Match list I of cell organelles with their functions in list II.

List I:
questions.solution:
The question refers to the specific function of Vacuoles.
  • In plant cells, vacuoles provide turgidity and rigidity and serve as storage for waste products and nutrients.

questions.question: Which food is a good source of complete protein?
questions.solution:
Eggs are a good source of complete protein.
  • A complete protein contains all nine essential amino acids that the human body cannot produce on its own. While plants like lentils have protein, they are often 'incomplete' unless paired with other foods.

questions.question: Muscle cells and muscle fibres are developed from embryonic precursor cells known as:
questions.solution:
Myoblasts are the embryonic precursor cells that differentiate to develop into muscle cells and muscle fibres.
  • During development, multiple myoblasts fuse together to form long, multinucleated muscle fibres.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered unicellular green algae?
questions.solution:
Chlamydomonas is a genus of unicellular green algae found in stagnant water and on damp soil.
  • It is a classic model organism in biology used to study photosynthesis and cell motility.

questions.question: Who first postulated that cells are generated from pre-existing cells?
questions.solution:
Rudolf Virchow first postulated 'Omnis cellula e cellula', meaning all cells are generated from pre-existing cells.
  • This became a fundamental tenet of the Cell Theory in 1855.

questions.question: The transportation mechanism in cells by which food or other useful molecules from the outside are carried inside the cell is known as _______________.
questions.solution:
Endocytosis is the mechanism by which cells engulf external material (food or molecules) by folding the cell membrane inward to form a vesicle.
  • Note: Exocytosis is the reverse process of moving materials out of the cell.

questions.question: A tunnel that runs through the cell wall between two plant cells is known as:
questions.solution:
A tunnel that runs through the cell wall between two plant cells is known as plasmodesmata.
  • (Note: This is a duplicate concept to question 12 in the set, emphasizing its importance in plant physiology).

questions.question: Which of the following are edible polysaccharides?
questions.solution:
Starch, alginates, pectins, and chitosans are all edible polysaccharides.
  • Starch is a primary energy source in human diets, while pectins and alginates are often used as thickening agents in the food industry.

questions.question: A particular cell present in the excretory system of flatworms, which helps them removing waste materials is the:
questions.solution:
Flame cells are specialized excretory cells found in flatworms (Platyhelminthes).
  • They function like a kidney, removing waste materials and regulating the water balance (osmoregulation) within the organism.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics was used by Aristotle to classify animals?
questions.solution:
Aristotle used habitat (land, water, or air) as one of his primary bases for classifying animals.
  • This was one of the earliest recorded systems of biological classification, though it has since been replaced by modern taxonomy.

questions.question: If the Glycemic Index (GI) of a specific food is from 70 to 100, then the type of that food is:
questions.solution:
A food with a Glycemic Index (GI) of 70 to 100 is classified as High-GI food.
  • High-GI foods cause a rapid spike in blood sugar levels. Examples include white bread, white rice, and sugary snacks.
